weaknesses.quote: At the next quarterly choice, if the previous note describes that action and nothing else intervened, a stat still below its `Expect` value goes into Stalled.
weaknesses.problem: The Expect and Stalled bookkeeping depends on exact values carried across turns, copied from displayed changes, and on judging whether anything else intervened. A model is unlikely to apply this reliably, and it is the most fragile part of the executable steps.
weaknesses.fix: Replace it with a simple rule: if the last quarterly action was X and the stat it was meant to raise did not rise by the next observe, skip that stat in the next quarter's choice. Drop the Expect field and the Stalled list.

weaknesses.quote: **Review in N:** N = 6 - (current_month mod 6), and N = 6 when current_month is a multiple of 6.
weaknesses.problem: The same skill says the review talk arrives as a new block starts at month 6, 12, 18. At month 6 the formula gives Review in 6, which contradicts a review happening at that point, so the review-close steps can fire at the wrong months.
weaknesses.fix: State it explicitly: at months 6, 12, 18 and so on the review is now (N = 0), and N = 1 applies at months 5, 11, 17 and so on. Check the table against the handbook's month-by-month schedule.

weaknesses.quote: challenging the company, its culture, leaders or rules even through a formal channel
weaknesses.problem: This states a hidden-risk mechanic as a likely effect with no published basis. The Skill's own disclaimer covers the 'working assumptions', but these lists are long and presented as likely effects, which falls under invented mechanics and weakens rules_match. Output and Network trading off is the same kind of claim.
weaknesses.fix: Mark the whole hidden-risk and stat-direction lists as the agent's own heuristics, keep only the directions the handbook states, and tell the agent to rely on the HR remark and the shown stat changes when they disagree with these heuristics.

weaknesses.quote: Missing a risky option costs far more than flagging a safe one: when in doubt, treat it as risky.
weaknesses.problem: This pushes the agent toward over-caution. Combined with the long hidden-risk list (which includes challenging leaders or rules through a formal channel), most options get dropped, so the agent may freeze or avoid legitimate growth choices across the 48 months.
weaknesses.fix: Calibrate the risk rule to the signals the game gives: treat an option as risky only when its text names a concrete hiding, denial, blame, shortcut or side-deal behaviour, and say that a neutral or reporting option is not risky.

weaknesses.quote: if the previous note describes that action and nothing else intervened, a stat still below its `Expect` value goes into Stalled
weaknesses.problem: The Stalled bookkeeping depends on comparing a previous note to observed stats and on judging whether something 'intervened'. A model reading many events per month will apply this inconsistently, and the Expect, Best, Stalled and Concerns fields make every turn heavy to execute.
weaknesses.fix: Cut the bookkeeping to what changes the decision: keep Stalled as a short list, define intervening as any story or HR event in the same quarter, and give one worked example of a single note and the next choice.

weaknesses.quote: The review talk arrives as a new six-month block starts (month 6, 12, 18 …), so the month before it (N = 1) is the last one whose choices count, and a single lost point there can cost the promotion.
weaknesses.problem: The timing of the review talk and the claim that month 47 is the last review-relevant month are stated as game facts. The handbook only says reviews happen every six months, so this is an invented mechanic presented as a rule and it drives the N = 1 exception in step 2 and the review-close step.
weaknesses.fix: Mark the timing as a working assumption, and tell the agent to confirm the review month from the observe events and to use the review talk as the trigger when they differ.

weaknesses.quote: The review talk arrives as a new six-month block starts (month 6, 12, 18 …), so the month before it (N = 1) is the last one whose choices count
weaknesses.problem: Presents an invented timing mechanic as a game fact. The published rules only say reviews occur every six months, not when the review talk arrives or which months count. Step 2's N = 1 exception depends on this claim, so the agent may take risks based on a rule that does not exist.
weaknesses.fix: Say that reviews fall at the six-month marks per the handbook, that the exact evaluation window is not published, and that N = 1 is a planning deadline for protecting Skill, Network and Output, not a hard cutoff for choices.

weaknesses.quote: A mild risk (handling something privately, partially or later) is then acceptable when it is the only way to keep Skill, Network and Output
weaknesses.problem: Contradicts itself. Step 2 allows private, partial or later handling in the review month, but step 4 says never to save a point by hiding a problem or cutting a corner, and the Story decisions section lists partial, phased and postponed fixes as risk. The agent gets two incompatible instructions in the month that matters most.
weaknesses.fix: Drop the mild-risk exception. Replace it with one rule: in N = 1 months, choose the option that keeps the three stats while still documenting or reporting the problem, and if none exists, pick the lowest-risk option and log it in Concerns.

weaknesses.quote: a provisional record of an expected gain that did not show up in this run
weaknesses.problem: The Stalled list, Expect values, Best values and Concerns counter all interact across turns and depend on the agent keeping exact bookkeeping. Under pressure the agent will misapply them, and the clarity and executable scores suffer as a result.
weaknesses.fix: Keep one simple rule: after an action has been chosen twice and the stat it should raise has not risen, add that stat to Stalled. Remove the Expect field and the Concerns counter, or reduce the Concerns counter to a single yes or no flag per month.

weaknesses.quote: The review talk arrives as a new six-month block starts (month 6, 12, 18 …), so the month before it (N = 1) is the last one whose choices count
weaknesses.problem: The Skill asserts timing for reviews and the 'last month that counts' as fact. The handbook only says a review happens every 6 months, and the Skill's own text says the pre-review timing is its own plan. Stating it this way risks misleading the agent. The N formula also disagrees with the claim that month 47 is a review month. The headline model of the whole Skill therefore rests on an unverified assumption.
weaknesses.fix: Label this clearly as a working assumption. Say the review happens every 6 months, with a review at month 6, 12 and so on, and tell the agent to correct the timing from what observe shows. Make the month-47 and month-48 statements agree with the N formula.

weaknesses.quote: Hidden risk (not shown; the HR remark is your only gauge) is likely to rise with hiding, denying, blaming, shortcuts, gambles, fixing things privately or off the record ... and challenging the company, its culture, leaders or rules even through a formal channel.
weaknesses.problem: A long list of invented effect mappings drives the choice steps, including the rule to treat anything uncertain as risky. They are flagged as assumptions, but they still steer almost every decision. They could over-penalise good options, and 'HR remark is your only gauge' is itself an unpublished claim. The Skill also relies on a named 'HR remark' with specific tones, which are tied to specific game wording.
weaknesses.fix: Cut the list down to a few general principles. State that effects must be read from the option text and from what the game shows after the choice. Make the risk heuristic simpler and symmetric rather than 'when in doubt treat as risky'. Drop the claim that the HR remark is the only gauge.

weaknesses.quote: Review in N | Now S<Skill> N<Network> O<Output> | Best S<..> N<..> O<..> | Stalled: none | Concerns this month: 0
weaknesses.problem: The bookkeeping scheme (Best, Stalled, Expect, Concerns, N) is heavy and fiddly for a small model. It is exposed to errors in copying and arithmetic, and it takes a lot of tokens in every note. The step order with its exceptions (the step 2 exception, the step 4 'skip if it would remove every option') is hard to follow. The result is long and dense, and the instructions are easy to misapply.
weaknesses.fix: Reduce the note to 2 or 3 fields: months until the review and the three stats. Drop Stalled and Concerns, or reduce them to one rule such as 'if a stat did not rise after two investments, switch'. Cut the decision procedure to 4 numbered priorities with no nested exceptions.

weaknesses.quote: Before choosing, read every option for the likely sign of its effect on Skill, Network, Output, Health, Dignity, Wealth and hidden risk. The game does not publish these effects; these are our working assumptions for reading option text
weaknesses.problem: The Skill leans heavily on invented keyword heuristics for story options (for example, 'Skill rises when you use your own judgement', 'challenging the company... even through a formal channel' raises hidden risk). Although flagged as assumptions, they steer most decisions and could mislead the agent. A rule that is wrong would be applied consistently, and the keyword lists can fail when event wording changes.
weaknesses.fix: Cut the keyword lists to a few principles that are safe (avoid hiding, blaming and shortcuts; prefer open, documented, full fixes). Tell the agent to update its beliefs from observed stat deltas and HR remarks, instead of pre-assigning signs to option text.

weaknesses.quote: The review talk arrives as a new six-month block starts (month 6, 12, 18 …), so the month before it (N = 1) is the last one whose choices count... The last review comes as month 48 starts, so month 47 is still a review month
weaknesses.problem: It states unpublished timing details as fact. The handbook lists review as step 9, after the quarterly phase of the same month. These claims are inconsistent with the published sequence and with the status-line formula, where N = 6 at month 6 and N = 1 at month 5. The agent may make wrong tradeoffs in months 5/11/... and 47, and in month 48.
weaknesses.fix: Follow the published sequence. Say that the review happens at the end of months 6, 12, ..., 48 after the quarterly phase, so the last quarterly phase before each review is in the same month. Remove the claims that month 47 is the last review month and that choices after month 47 don't count.

weaknesses.quote: `Review in N | Now S<Skill> N<Network> O<Output> | Best S<..> N<..> O<..> | Stalled: none | Concerns this month: 0`
weaknesses.problem: The status-line bookkeeping (Best, Stalled, Expect, Concerns, N) is heavy for a flash-class model. Together with a multi-step story procedure with many exceptions (step 2 exception vs step 4, 'skip a step if it would remove every option'), it is easy to get wrong, and the Skill is long and dense. Clarity and token cost suffer.
weaknesses.fix: Reduce the note to a short line (month, N, the three stats, last HR remark). Drop Stalled, Expect and Concerns, or fold them into one rule such as 'if a stat did not rise after an action meant to raise it, try another'. Cut the nested exceptions to a flat priority list.

weaknesses.quote: Review in N:** N = 6 - (current_month mod 6), and N = 6 when current_month is a multiple of 6. ... The review talk arrives as a new six-month block starts (month 6, 12, 18 …), so the month before it (N = 1) is the last one whose choices count
weaknesses.problem: The review timing is inconsistent and invented. The handbook says the review comes every 6 months, and the Skill treats it as happening at the start of month 7, 13 and so on. It then calls month 47 the last review month, yet month 48 is a quarterly phase. The mandatory status-line arithmetic adds error risk, and the review cadence is presented as established fact when it is not.
weaknesses.fix: State only what is published: reviews every 6 months, at months 6, 12, …, 48. Drop the off-by-one framing. Replace N with a simple rule: 'in the 2 months before month 6k, protect Skill, Network and Output'.

weaknesses.quote: `Review in N | Now S<Skill> N<Network> O<Output> | Best S<..> N<..> O<..> | Stalled: none | Concerns this month: 0`
weaknesses.problem: The status-line bookkeeping is heavy: Best, Stalled, Expect and Concerns, with reset rules, copied by hand into every note. It is a lot of overhead for a flash-class model, it adds token cost, and it breaks easily if a note is lost. The Stalled mechanism can also wrongly stop investing in a stat because of noisy or hidden-event changes.
weaknesses.fix: Cut the note to one short line, such as 'Review in N | S/N/O | HR remark'. Delete Best, Stalled, Expect and Concerns, and use the plain rule 'if a stat fell since the last quarter, prioritise it'.

weaknesses.quote: **Hidden risk** (not shown; the HR remark is your only gauge) is likely to rise with hiding, denying, blaming, shortcuts, gambles, ... and challenging the company, its culture, leaders or rules even through a formal channel.
weaknesses.problem: A long list of undeclared effect mappings is built on assumptions. It is labelled as assumptions, but it still drives hard filtering rules such as dropping options and 'when in doubt, treat it as risky'. The 'HR remark' tiers and the 'last month before a review' exception are also not backed by the published rules. The Skill is dense and has many nested rules, which makes it hard to follow when event wording varies.
weaknesses.fix: Reduce the mappings to a few general principles (be honest, document, avoid shortcuts, protect Health and Dignity). Present the rest as soft tie-breakers, not hard drops. Cut the nested exceptions to two or three clear priority rules.

weaknesses.quote: Skill is the only one of the three that a quarter can raise directly through two published actions (Skill learning, Apply for rotation); the other two also come from stories.
weaknesses.problem: Misstates the published rules. Apply for a key project and Build a mentorship also raise Skill. Output and Network are raised directly by several quarterly actions (Prepare report materials, Fight for resources, Network maintenance, Report results to your manager).
weaknesses.fix: List every quarterly action that raises Skill, and state that Output and Network also have direct quarterly actions, so the Skill-first plan is a choice rather than a necessity.

weaknesses.quote: Anything else (frowning, uneasy, "you are on your own", angry): first Energy action Defuse legacy risk and main action Lay low and reduce risk, every quarter until the remark is friendly or quiet again.
weaknesses.problem: Defuse legacy risk has no published effect, and Lay low and reduce risk only raises Health. Applied every quarter with no cap, this can starve Output, Skill and Network indefinitely, and the Energy cost of 2 is spent on an unpublished effect presented as the cure.
weaknesses.fix: Say that Defuse legacy risk's effect is unpublished. Cap the risk-only response at about two quarters, then return one quarter to a growth main action such as Repair a key relationship or Report results to your manager.

weaknesses.quote: Review in N | Now S<Skill> N<Network> O<Output> | Best S<..> N<..> O<..> | Stalled: none | Concerns this month: 0
weaknesses.problem: The required bookkeeping (Best, Stalled, Concerns, recalled across months through check_latest_logs) is error-prone for a single agent. The Stalled rule depends on an 'expected gain' the agent cannot measure, so the chain of notes is hard to keep accurate and may drive the wrong choices.
weaknesses.fix: Keep only Review in N, the current three stats, and a short list of stats to protect. Drop the Concerns counter, or track it inside the reasoning for the current month, and define Stalled with one concrete trigger, such as two quarters with no rise after a paid action.

weaknesses.quote: Skill is the only one of the three that a quarter can raise directly through two published actions (Skill learning, Apply for rotation); the other two also come from stories.
weaknesses.problem: Factually wrong against the published tables. Skill also rises from Apply for a key project and Build a mentorship. Network and Output also have several published actions (Network maintenance, Repair a key relationship, Report results to your manager, Prepare report materials, Showcase results). The stated justification for the senior-level Skill plan is therefore invented.
weaknesses.fix: Delete the claim, or replace it with a correct per-stat list of published actions taken from rules.rst, and justify the Skill priority only by the stated game rules.

weaknesses.quote: If Dignity is not near the top of its range (our margin: 7 or below), drop options that lower it
weaknesses.problem: Dignity is at or below 7 for most of a run, so this step removes nearly every option that lowers Dignity in every month. It overrides the Grow step and pushes the agent toward passivity, which the rubric's 'strategy matches the rules' criterion does not support.
weaknesses.fix: Use a stricter margin such as 3 or below, or make it a tie-breaker in step 5 rather than a hard filter.

weaknesses.quote: with the friendly remark, three 1-cost actions: Health recovery and Mental recovery while either is below full, then Network maintenance.
weaknesses.problem: The Energy sequence is ambiguous and not executable. If both Health and Dignity are full, or only one is below full, the count of actions to take is unclear, and the rule does not say what to do with leftover Energy.
weaknesses.fix: Write an explicit order: Network maintenance first, then Health recovery if Health is below 10, then Mental recovery if Dignity is below 10, stopping at 3 points; state that unspent Energy is lost.

weaknesses.quote: Skill is the only one of the three that a quarter can raise directly through two published actions (Skill learning, Apply for rotation); the other two also come from stories.
weaknesses.problem: Factually wrong against the published tables. Apply for a key project and Build a mentorship also raise Skill, and Network and Output have their own Energy and main actions. The claim is presented as a published fact and drives the senior-level plan.
weaknesses.fix: Delete the claim, or replace it with a list of every published action that raises each of Skill, Network and Output, citing the handbook tables.

weaknesses.quote: The review talk arrives as a new six-month block starts (month 6, 12, 18 …), so the month before it (N = 1) is the last one whose choices count, and a single lost point there can cost the promotion.
weaknesses.problem: Invented timing presented as game mechanics. The handbook says only that a formal review occurs every six months and that promotion depends on sustained results, not on a cut-off month. The 'last one whose choices count' rule is unpublished and the agent may over-weight that month.
weaknesses.fix: State that the review cadence is published but the evaluation window is not, and that the last months before a review are a precaution rather than a known cut-off.

weaknesses.quote: and challenging the company, its culture, leaders or rules even through a formal channel.
weaknesses.problem: An unsupported hidden-risk claim. It is not in the published rules, and combined with 'when in doubt, treat it as risky' it could make the agent avoid legitimate formal escalation the game may reward.
weaknesses.fix: Remove the clause. Tell the agent to rely on the HR remark and warnings as the only risk gauge, and to prefer documented, formal, process-following options when a real problem exists.

weaknesses.quote: `Review in N | Now S<Skill> N<Network> O<Output> | Best S<..> N<..> O<..> | Stalled: none | Concerns this month: 0`
weaknesses.problem: The status-line bookkeeping (Best, Stalled, Concerns, N arithmetic) is heavy and invented. It must be recomputed every turn by a small model. It adds many chances for error and uses up context, and the Skill's sections cross-reference each other so much that it is hard to follow.
weaknesses.fix: Cut the note to a short memory, such as 'Review in N | stat trend | last HR remark'. Drop Best, Stalled and Concerns. Keep the quarterly decision rules as a simple priority list.

weaknesses.quote: The review talk arrives as a new six-month block starts (month 6, 12, 18 …), so the month before it (N = 1) is the last one whose choices count
weaknesses.problem: The rules say the review happens every six months. They do not say which months' choices count or when the review talk arrives. This invented timing is presented as fact, and the N = 1 'mild risk' exception depends on it. The same exception tells the agent to accept hidden risk in order to protect a promotion, which conflicts with the Skill's own risk-first guidance and with the handbook's warning that landmines compound.
weaknesses.fix: Say that the review falls every six months and that Skill, Network and Output are cumulative. Replace the N = 1 exception with 'build these stats steadily every quarter'. Remove the instruction to accept hidden risk.

weaknesses.quote: Skill learning (2) while Health is above 6 (our margin), then one point (1) on Network maintenance ... Main action Apply for rotation. This line holds for the rest of the career
weaknesses.problem: The fixed margins (Health above 6, Dignity 7 or below, 4 or below) and the rigid 'first matching line wins' quarterly ladder are invented thresholds. A fixed recipe for level 4 and above, with Output neglected, may leave Output behind and may overspend Health. Wealth is barely planned across the 48 months.
weaknesses.fix: Describe the quarterly choice as a balanced priority: recover whatever is critical, then reduce risk, then raise the weakest of Skill, Network and Output. Give margins as soft guidance. Add a short plan for wealth and for the stat mix by phase of the career.

weaknesses.quote: Review in N | Now S<Skill> N<Network> O<Output> | Best S<..> N<..> O<..> | Stalled: none | Concerns this month: 0
weaknesses.problem: The status-line bookkeeping (Best, Stalled, Concerns, N) is heavy for a small flash model. It adds a long, error-prone memory layer, and the 'Stalled' mechanism is an invented system that can wrongly rule out useful stats. Together with the 5-step story procedure and 6-line quarterly cascade, the document is dense and hard to follow consistently.
weaknesses.fix: Cut the note to 'Review in N | S/N/O now | HR remark'. Drop Best, Stalled and Concerns. Keep the 5-step story order but shorten each step to one line.

weaknesses.quote: The review talk arrives as a new six-month block starts (month 6, 12, 18 …), so the month before it (N = 1) is the last one whose choices count
weaknesses.problem: The review timing is asserted as fact, and the Skill is internally inconsistent. N=1 is defined as the month before a review, yet it also says month 47 is the last review month and the review comes 'as month 48 starts'. The handbook only says the review is every 6 months. Many 'working assumptions' (option-text effect signs, margins of 4 and 7, 'friendly' HR remark tiers) are presented in confident rules language and could mislead the agent.
weaknesses.fix: State only the published cadence: a review every 6 months, at months 6, 12 and so on. Define N as months until the next multiple of 6, and mark every margin and effect sign as a heuristic to be overridden by observed stat changes.

weaknesses.quote: Missing a risky option costs far more than flagging a safe one: when in doubt, treat it as risky.
weaknesses.problem: This pushes the agent to over-avoid risk and to cut stat-raising options. Together with 'Defuse legacy risk' every quarter on any non-friendly remark, it can crowd out growth (Skill, Network, Output) and hurt promotion and wealth over 48 months. There is no explicit pacing or milestone plan for early, mid and late game, and no rule for when the agent stops defusing.
weaknesses.fix: Add a phased plan (months 1-12 build Skill and Network, 13-36 push promotions, 37-48 consolidate). Cap Defuse legacy risk at once per quarter and only when the remark worsens or warnings appear. Say what to do when every option is risky.

weaknesses.quote: Reviews come every six months (handbook); N = 1 is the last month before a review, the deadline for review preparation in our plan.
weaknesses.problem: The Skill invents mechanics presented as operational fact. It says the review talk arrives at month 6, 12 and so on, that the choices in the month before it are the ones that count, and that 'a single lost point there can cost the promotion'. It also says month 47 is still a review month. The handbook only says a review happens every 6 months, and does not say which months' choices are counted. These claims are asserted rather than labelled as assumptions. The month-47 and month-48 handling is also internally inconsistent.
weaknesses.fix: Label the review-timing claims as assumptions. Use a simple rule based only on published facts: keep Skill, Network and Output rising steadily, and avoid harmful choices in the months before each six-month boundary.

weaknesses.quote: `Review in N | Now S<Skill> N<Network> O<Output> | Best S<..> N<..> O<..> | Stalled: none | Concerns this month: 0`
weaknesses.problem: The Skill is very long and dense. The status-line bookkeeping (Best, Stalled, Concerns, N) carries a lot of state and has many special cases. Together with the nested step 2 exception and step 4 N=1/N=2 variants, a flash-class model is likely to execute it inconsistently. The agent also pays token cost on every note and has to re-read the rules each turn.
weaknesses.fix: Cut the note to a short status of Review in N plus Health, Dignity, Skill, Network and Output. Drop Best, Stalled and Concerns. Reduce the story procedure to 4 or 5 short priority rules.

weaknesses.quote: Skill **rises** when you use your own judgement: analyse, bring data or evidence ... **Output** rises when you deliver, ship, finish ... Missing a risky option costs far more than flagging a safe one: when in doubt, treat it as risky.
weaknesses.problem: Long keyword heuristics that map option wording to hidden effects are invented mechanics. They are only labelled as 'working assumptions'. Several are overconfident, such as 'challenging the company even through a formal channel' being risky. They may be wrong or misleading, and they are brittle when event wording changes. The thresholds (Health 4, Dignity 7, Health 6) are arbitrary and uncited. Dignity at 7 or below being treated as 'low' means almost every option is dropped by step 3.
weaknesses.fix: Replace the keyword lists with a few principles: prefer transparent, complete, process-following options; avoid concealment and shortcuts; weigh the displayed stat changes shown after each choice. Set thresholds from published ranges with explicit rationale, for example Dignity at 4 or below, and say to relax them when every option fails.
